log.msg: read requirements.md, review.md, data.json, task.jsonl, readme.md, servex/page.js; investigating sidebar duplicate Overview/Docs cause via Explore agent before editing

sidebar duplicate Overview/Docs traced (Explore agent): ux/Tree.js nodes_of() draws sidebar rows straight off page.children, and Doc.js's overview_section()/docs_section() add Overview/Docs into that same children map as ordinary pages -- so Servex's OWN Overview/Docs tabs sit right below Lifecycle's subtree in the tree, reading as a duplicate. This is general Tree.js/Doc.js behavior across every Doc page with a Doc-typed child, not caused by lifecycle/page.js's own children (it declares none) -- out of my fence (ux/Tree.js, ext/Doc/Doc.js). Per the brief's own conditional ('if it comes from this page's own children') I'm leaving this one to a framework-level fix and noting it here instead.

Rewrote lifecycle/page.js: before->after row (wrappers 20->9, idle agents 14->4; tasks/worktrees keep study-only counts, no after -- reaper doesn't touch either), one line naming the 18:03 sweep and the run.js/node sub-counts (finding 3+6). Chart now memory-only (servers+idle agents), worktree disk called out as a separate sentence instead of a bar (finding 5). Pool section cut to two lines linking Servex/doc/pool.md and Servex/doc/lifecycle.md as plain code refs, not URLs -- Servex/ isn't served statically, confirmed both link paths 404 on first try and fixed to plain backtick text (finding 4). readme.md's stale 'reaper doesn't exist yet' watch-out line replaced with what it does now (finding 2).

Layout (findings 10/11): numbers row + chart were stacking, not side by side, at both 1920 and 3440 -- traced to core/Page's default reading-column cap (--measure: 40em on the outer .flow div, ~640px), the same mechanism core/Page/doc/css.md documents an opt-out for. Added .wide to the top-level wrapper; re-shot and confirmed both widths now show numbers+chart side by side above the fold, worst-ten table below.

Two findings traced but left unfixed, both out of my two-file fence (public/framework/servex/lifecycle/ and public/framework/servex/page.js), logged for a framework-level fix: (a) page heading reads 'Servex' not 'Lifecycle' -- ext/Doc/Doc.js's bar() puts every declared child of a Doc page into the PARENT's own tab strip, sharing the parent's single h1; lifecycle is a tab of Servex's Doc shell, not a standalone routed page. (b) duplicate Overview/Docs in the sidebar -- ux/Tree.js draws sidebar rows straight off page.children, and Doc.js adds its own Overview/Docs into that same children map, so Servex's own Overview/Docs sit right below Lifecycle's subtree. Neither comes from lifecycle/page.js's own children (it declares none), matching the brief's own conditional to leave it. Fixing either means editing ext/Doc/Doc.js or ux/Tree.js, which changes every Doc-typed module on the site.

servex/page.js finding 12: replaced the bottom 'How much is left running' section with one bullet in 'Its parts' linking Lifecycle -- no longer repeats the Lifecycle tab or falls below the fold at 1920.
